'''''Odontonema tubaeforme''''' is a plant in the family [[Acanthaceae]] native to [[Central America]] and [[Naturalization|naturalised]] as a [[Introduced species|garden escape]] in numerous other countries.

==Description==
''O. tubaeforme'' is an upright shrub up to 2 m<ref>Fosberg et al., 1993; pp. 33-34</ref> or 3 m<ref>(Smith, 1991; p. 135).</ref> tall. Its elliptical, glossy leaves are 10 cm by 20 cm with a 2 cm petiole and arranged opposite each other on the stem.<ref name=":2" /> It has terminal spikes of waxy red to burgundy flowers, 30 mm long with 5 mm petals,<ref name=":2" /> and blooms in summer and autumn.<ref name=":1" /> It is grown as an annual frost-tender ornamental garden plant.<ref name=":0" /><gallery mode="packed" heights="130" caption="''O. tubaeforme'' in cultivation">

==Range==
[[File:Odontonema tubiforme (Bertol.) Kuntze (AM AK360518).jpg|thumb|Naturalised ''O. tubaeforme'' collected at [[Kaitaia]] in the collection of [[Auckland War Memorial Museum]].]]
''O. tubaeforme'' is native to Central America,<ref>[http://www.hear.org/pier/species/odontonema_tubaeforme.htm Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk (PIER)]</ref> but has naturalised in several countries as an ornamental garden plant, including New Zealand and Australia. Since 2005 it has been recorded in the wild in the far north of New Zealand, at [[Auckland]], [[Kaitaia]], and [[Doubtless Bay]]. In New Zealand it usually spreads through the dumping of garden waste, although in one locality ([[Taipa-Mangonui|Cooper's Beach]]) seedlings have been found.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Odontonema tubaeforme|url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/odontonema-tubaeforme/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network|language=en}}</ref> In the Pacific it is considered an [[invasive species]], and has recently naturalised in [[Rarotonga]] and [[Mangaia]] in the [[Cook Islands]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Odontonema tubiforme - Odontonema|url=http://cookislands.bishopmuseum.org/species.asp?id=6450|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Cook Islands Biodiversity}}</ref>

==Name==
The genus name "''Odontonema''" refers to the toothed filaments of the [[stamen]], ''nema'' meaning "thread" and ''odonto'' "toothed".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=''Odontonema tubaeforme'' (Firespike)|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/odontonema-tubaeforme/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-20|website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox}}</ref> In English this species is known as '''cardinal flower''', '''cardinal's guard''', or '''fire spike'''.<ref name=":0" />
